executive_summary: **Executive summary:** The version picture that has dogged the week finally sharpens — and launch momentum carries it. The [News feed](/?date=2026-10-12&category=news) now treats **Hermes Agent v0.21.6** as the current stable, and its top story is an operator's guide — "[**Hermes Agent v0.21.6: Dashboard Auth, Git Filter and Email Sender Fixes**](/?date=2026-10-12&category=news#item-a3e3807260aa)" — covering **dashboard authentication** hardening, a **git filter** lockdown, and an **email sender** fix, must-read material for anyone running production. The **v0.21.7** train stays hot with four same-day RCs, **[rc.10](/?date=2026-10-12&category=news#item-cbe579ccb9b5)** through **rc.13** (**[rc.11](/?date=2026-10-12&category=news#item-c19a22c9ff13)** the freshest representative; the feed itself filtered the **rc.12**–**rc.13** write-ups as redundant, so cite the range rather than chase individual tags) — an imminent stable drop remains the live signal. The research feed's canonical [**v0.20.0** release notes](/?date=2026-10-11&category=research#item-hn-49159200) (tag **v2026.8.3**) read as official-docs catch-up — and by pairing the version with its date-style tag they all but resolve the long-running **v2026.8.3** discrepancy — while the **[Claude Pro/Max](/?date=2026-10-12&category=research#item-hn-49790991)** subscription docs (now surfaced under the **claude-subscription-directsdk** plugin name) are likewise catch-up on carried support, not a fresh launch. Social is celebratory and builder-heavy: **@NousResearch**'s terse "[Hermes Agent is yours](/?date=2026-10-12&category=social)" launch post (2,535 likes) headlines the cycle, and **@Teknium**'s "[fun with Hermes](/?date=2026-10-12&category=social#item-63d9c6a50959)" teaser drew the batch's biggest reach (~1,420 likes, ~82K views). The new infrastructure story is official skills/plugins plumbing: **@Teknium** announced [official plugins are consolidating into a **mono-repo**](/?date=2026-10-12&category=social#item-b2da2d2b0312) for centralized issue tracking, confirmed the [**anatomy skill**](/?date=2026-10-12&category=social#item-f63377423812) (wireframes and interactive prototypes) as an officially integrated optional skill, and publicly [asked **@wheresryan22** for permission](/?date=2026-10-12&category=social#item-0f5b54d8981d) to promote their community creation to a built-in — a permission-first adoption pipeline readers received warmly. He also set the contribution model explicitly: [no direct contributors — ship a plugin for the catalog instead](/?date=2026-10-12&category=social#item-29cc3440078a), and [only Nous-created/maintained plugins count as official](/?date=2026-10-12&category=social#item-b8ffcffb6f26). Third-party momentum: **@rlaope** shipped [**Oh-My-Hermes 3.0.2**](/?date=2026-10-12&category=social#item-d889c32305ce), adding **SkillEx** and **FenceGuard** and framing Hermes Agent as a multi-model team with skills, routing, and long-term memory — while transparently [spinning up another worker node](/?date=2026-10-12&category=social#item-a1bfa0dbd79e) after a traffic surge and clarifying the **~1,000 TPS** figure is peak, not average. The community showcase is **TOTS (Thoughts On Terminal Screen)** — an [open-source, Love, Death & Robots-inspired screensaver](/?date=2026-10-12&category=news#item-876bf1b2193c) that passively visualizes your agent's reasoning, responses, and tool activity — a real monitoring pain point, solved with style. **@Teknium** also handled rumor control: "[beyond all doubt](/?date=2026-10-12&category=social#item-1c7ba80e94e8)," a tracker-attributed model is not Nous's, and [it isn't a router either](/?date=2026-10-12&category=social#item-f8dd7db72030) — firm, good-natured myth-busting. Research watch: **@hardmaru** surfaced [Sakana AI's **MASS** paper](/?date=2026-10-12&category=social#item-d648c1b54651) — recursive self-improvement via multi-agent self-supervision, [framed through Minsky's Society of Mind](/?date=2026-10-12&category=social#item-37fbc6f41417) — reporting a **27B** open-weights model improving [**1.2–1.6x** per output token after two cycles](/?date=2026-10-12&category=social#item-84c0404d433d), an open-weights result that lands well with this community and rhymes with the carried [**Refine Cycle** self-improvement plugin](/?date=2026-10-12&category=research#item-hn-49606988). Carried, not new: [**Hermes Kanban**](/?date=2026-10-11&category=research#item-hn-49604068), [**LanceDB** semantic memory](/?date=2026-10-11&category=research#item-hn-49133145), [**verso**](/?date=2026-10-11&category=research#item-hn-49628094), [**Grafana**](/?date=2026-10-11&category=research#item-hn-49318128), the [**Kubernetes** gaps](/?date=2026-10-11&category=research#item-hn-49977400) (no official **Helm** chart; **root-at-init** image), the [**Arduino UNO Q**](/?date=2026-10-11&category=research#item-hn-49368474) hobbyist host, the [**~23,000 open-PR** backlog](/?date=2026-10-11&category=research#item-hn-49424643), and [**Almanac (YC S26)**](/?date=2026-10-11&category=research#item-hn-49511007) again topping research ("Launch HN: AI that knows your company"). Fresher on the ops side: a [headless-Debian debugging walkthrough](/?date=2026-10-12&category=research#item-hn-49916751) with captured traces and a [**Bifrost** model-router reliability discussion](/?date=2026-10-12&category=research#item-hn-49159529) — the former repeats the caution that its "**GLM 5.3 Flash**" reference stays unverified against the confirmed Z.ai catalog, which tops out at **GLM-5.2** (2026-06-16). Housekeeping: Reddit contributed nothing again; the routine [daily repo sync](/?date=2026-10-12&category=news#item-b093d6f7db37) and off-topic [listicles](/?date=2026-10-12&category=research#item-ecaec348555b)/[trademark threads](/?date=2026-10-12&category=research#item-hn-49357715) were filtered as noise. One carried deadline bears repeating precisely because it's three days out: [three memory providers leave Hermes Agent core on **2026-10-15**](/?date=2026-10-11&category=news#item-d96f0bcb45e6) — migrate external backends (e.g., **Honcho**) now. Net read: no stable **v0.21.7** yet, but **v0.21.6**'s confirmation plus a same-day four-RC burst say it's close — the cycle's real story is official infrastructure absorbing community creations under a clear contribution model, with security hardening leading the stable line.

This is the week's central storyline across all content categories.

top_topics.name: Skills and Plugin Ecosystem
top_topics.description: Official and community plugin infrastructure is expanding rapidly: [official plugins are consolidating into a mono-repo for centralized issue tracking](/?date=2026-10-12&category=social#item-b2da2d2b0312), [the anatomy skill became an officially integrated optional skill](/?date=2026-10-12&category=social#item-f63377423812), and [Teknium is adopting community creations through a permission-first pipeline](/?date=2026-10-12&category=social#item-0f5b54d8981d). Third-party layers like [Oh-My-Hermes 3.0.2 (SkillEx, FenceGuard)](/?date=2026-10-12&category=social#item-d889c32305ce) and projects like [Refine Cycle](/?date=2026-10-12&category=research#item-hn-49606988) and [verso](/?date=2026-10-12&category=research#item-hn-49628094) show a maturing extension ecosystem. The contribution model is also being clarified - [ship a plugin for the catalog rather than contributing directly](/?date=2026-10-12&category=social#item-29cc3440078a), with [only Nous-created and maintained plugins counting as official](/?date=2026-10-12&category=social#item-b8ffcffb6f26).

top_topics.name: Memory and Multi-Agent Orchestration
top_topics.description: Persistence and coordination capabilities are advancing together, with [LanceDB-backed semantic memory](/?date=2026-10-12&category=research#item-hn-49133145) for durable recall and the new [Hermes Kanban multi-agent profile collaboration](/?date=2026-10-12&category=research#item-hn-49604068). [Oh-My-Hermes](/?date=2026-10-12&category=social#item-d889c32305ce) similarly positions the agent as a multi-model team with routing and long-term memory. Adjacent research such as [Sakana's MASS](/?date=2026-10-12&category=social#item-d648c1b54651) frames multi-agent self-supervision as the path to continual capability gains.

Deployment documentation also exposes a security-relevant gap with a [root-at-init container image on Kubernetes](/?date=2026-10-12&category=research#item-hn-49977400). Operators running production deployments are the clear audience for this theme.

top_topics.name: Deployment and Self-Hosting Practices
top_topics.description: Self-hosting guidance is maturing but reveals real operational gaps: no official Helm chart, root-privileged containers on Kubernetes, and a headless-Debian debugging walkthrough with captured traces. Low-cost hardware recipes like running the agent on an [Arduino UNO Q](/?date=2026-10-12&category=research#item-hn-49368474) highlight grassroots experimentation. Production-readiness [documentation](/?date=2026-10-12&category=news#item-a3e3807260aa) is emerging as a visible community need.

top_topics.name: Agent Observability and Monitoring
top_topics.description:
Visualizing what an agent is doing is an emerging need, addressed by TOTS (Thoughts On Terminal Screen), an open-source Love, Death & Robots-inspired screensaver that passively renders reasoning, responses, and tool activity. A Grafana dashboard integration fills the same observability gap for metrics-minded operators. Both solve the common pain point of limited visibility into agent behavior.

top_topics.name: External Integrations and Model Routing
top_topics.description: Hermes is increasingly positioned within a broader coding-agent stack, with [reproducible skill loops pairing it with Codex and Claude Code](/?date=2026-10-12&category=research#item-hn-49136162), and a [claude-subscription-directsdk plugin enabling Claude Pro/Max subscription access](/?date=2026-10-12&category=research#item-hn-49790991) instead of API keys. Reliability discussions around the [Bifrost model router](/?date=2026-10-12&category=research#item-hn-49159529) even ask whether the agent is usable without multi-model routing. Integration with external providers and routers is becoming a core expectation.

top_items.title: I made a Love, Death & Robots-inspired screensaver to see what my AI agent is doing
top_items.content: I've been working on TOTS (Thoughts On Terminal Screen), a small open-source screensaver for Hermes Agent. I have an old laptop for my Hermes Agent that stays on my desk, and I wanted a way to see what my agent was doing without constantly checking the terminal or Telegram. TOTS listens to the agent's reasoning, responses, and tool activity, turning them into scrolling pixelated emojis. The animation is inspired by the title sequences of Love, Death & Robots. The idea is pretty simple: while the agent is working, the display keeps moving. When it becomes idle, the animation gradually settles down. It's meant to be something you can notice in your peripheral vision without demanding your attention. It started as an experiment inspired by GERTY from Moon, but I eventually moved away from facial expressions and ended up with this terminal-based approach. It supports custom themes, multiple sessions and subagents, and a debug mode that shows in real time what's going on in the background. Under the hood, a small plugin streams events through a local socket. Short phrases are matched against a customizable CSV to select emojis. You can also provide your own Python converter if you want something more sophisticated.  No extra AI inference needed.  Offline/Local friendly & Open source. GitHub: https://github.com/anderson-/TOTS I'd be interested to hear what you think, especially about the visual approach.    submitted by    /u/_apekind_    to    r/hermesagent   [link]   [comments]

research.category_summary: Research and documentation this cycle centers on official capability expansion and a maturing self-hosting ecosystem. Headline items: official docs for **[Claude Pro/Max subscription](/?date=2026-10-12&category=research#item-hn-49790991)** support via the **claude-subscription-directsdk** plugin (reuse existing Anthropic plans instead of API keys) and the canonical **[Hermes Agent v0.20.0](/?date=2026-10-12&category=research#item-hn-49159200)** release notes (tag **v2026.8.3**). Orchestration and memory advance together: the new **[Hermes Kanban](/?date=2026-10-12&category=research#item-hn-49604068)** multi-agent profile collaboration, **[LanceDB](/?date=2026-10-12&category=research#item-hn-49133145)**-backed semantic memory for persistent recall, and the **[Refine Cycle](/?date=2026-10-12&category=research#item-hn-49606988)** self-improvement plugin. Deployment documentation exposes real operational gaps — no official **Helm** chart and a root-at-init container image on **[Kubernetes](/?date=2026-10-12&category=research#item-hn-49977400)**, a [headless-Debian debugging walkthrough](/?date=2026-10-12&category=research#item-hn-49916751) with captured traces, and a low-cost **[Arduino UNO Q](/?date=2026-10-12&category=research#item-hn-49368474)** host recipe. Production tooling fills observability and routing needs: a **[Grafana](/?date=2026-10-12&category=research#item-hn-49318128)** dashboard integration, the **[verso](/?date=2026-10-12&category=research#item-hn-49628094)** open-source orchestrator for knowledge work, and a **[Bifrost](/?date=2026-10-12&category=research#item-hn-49159529)** model-router reliability discussion. Ecosystem health reads strong but strained: ~**[23,000 open PRs](/?date=2026-10-12&category=research#item-hn-49424643)** signal rapid community growth, **[Almanac (YC S26)](/?date=2026-10-12&category=research#item-hn-49511007)** validates enterprise demand for tamed Hermes deployments, and reproducible skill loops pairing Hermes with **[Codex and Claude Code](/?date=2026-10-12&category=research#item-hn-49136162)** show where multi-agent coding workflows are heading. Verification note: the debugging thread's '**[GLM 5.3 Flash](/?date=2026-10-12&category=research#item-hn-49916751)**' does not match our verified Z.ai catalog (latest confirmed release is **GLM-5.2**, 2026-06-16) — treat that model name as unverified. Off-topic items (a Claude Code earnings-data plugin, a trademark thread, personal usage reflections, and two promotional SEO/Skool listicles) were excluded from the ranking.

social.category_summary: **Agent launch & momentum:** **NousResearch**'s terse '[Hermes Agent is yours](/?date=2026-10-12&category=social#item-d586a63d28e6)' post was the week's headline (2,535 likes), and **Teknium** kept hype high with a cryptic '[fun with Hermes](/?date=2026-10-12&category=social#item-63d9c6a50959)' teaser that drew the batch's biggest reach (~1,420 likes, ~82K views) — sentiment is celebratory and builder-heavy. **Official skills & plugin infrastructure:** **Teknium** announced [official plugins are consolidating into a mono-repo](/?date=2026-10-12&category=social#item-b2da2d2b0312) for centralized issue tracking, confirmed the **[anatomy skill](/?date=2026-10-12&category=social#item-f63377423812)** for wireframes and interactive prototypes as an officially integrated optional skill, and publicly asked **[@wheresryan22](/?date=2026-10-12&category=social#item-0f5b54d8981d)** for permission to promote their community creation to a built-in skill — a community-to-official pipeline readers responded to warmly. He also set the contribution model: [no direct contributors, ship a plugin for the catalog instead](/?date=2026-10-12&category=social#item-29cc3440078a), and [only Nous-created/maintained plugins count as official](/?date=2026-10-12&category=social#item-b8ffcffb6f26). **Ecosystem tooling:** **rlaope** released **[Oh-My-Hermes 3.0.2](/?date=2026-10-12&category=social#item-d889c32305ce)** adding **SkillEx** and **FenceGuard**, turning Hermes Agent into a multi-model team with skills, routing, and long-term memory, and transparently reported [spinning up another worker node after a traffic surge](/?date=2026-10-12&category=social#item-a1bfa0dbd79e) (1,000 TPS is peak, not average) — a strong organic-growth signal for the third-party ecosystem. **Rumor control:** **Teknium** stated ['beyond all doubt' that a tracker-attributed model is not Nous's](/?date=2026-10-12&category=social#item-1c7ba80e94e8) and separately [ruled out it being a router](/?date=2026-10-12&category=social#item-f8dd7db72030) — firm, good-natured myth-busting that the community appreciated. **Research watch:** **hardmaru**'s Sakana AI **[MASS paper](/?date=2026-10-12&category=social#item-d648c1b54651)** (recursive self-improvement via multi-agent self-supervision, framed through [Minsky's Society of Mind](/?date=2026-10-12&category=social#item-37fbc6f41417)) reports a [27B open-weights model improving 1.2–1.6x per output token after two cycles](/?date=2026-10-12&category=social#item-84c0404d433d) — findings that resonate with the open-weights ethos of the Hermes community. Overall: a launch-week feed dominated by official momentum, an active skills/plugins culture, and credible adjacent research.

top_items.content:
Oh-My-Hermes 3.0.2 Released! SkillEx & FenceGuard

OMH: https://t.co/g1exHwWK5E

Oh-My-Hermes turns Hermes Agent into a team: ready-made skills, a router that picks the right one for every message, long-term memory, and sandboxed parallel coding agents across GPT, Claude, DeepSeek, Kimi and GLM.

SkillEx: skills that work more carefully

- Quoting is safe. Pasting a message that mentions a workflow no longer starts that workflow.
- Plans point out what is still untested before any code is written.
- Debugging stops after three failed fixes and looks at the bigger design instead of guessing again.
- Long-running loops agree on a clear finish line and the files they must not touch before they start.
- A new test has to catch a real bug before it counts.
- Small in-scope decisions are made and written down without stopping to ask you, and review rounds are capped.
- "Yes" means what you said yes to. Agreeing to an idea doesn't approve the whole plan.
- Debugging a past session is read-only.
- Backend work keeps one source of truth for each API contract.

FenceGuard: parallel agents stay in their sandbox

- Parallel coding agents never run outside their sandbox unless you allow it.
- Inside the sandbox they get no credentials and no network.
- An agent can't plant settings that later run on your machine.
- A run that never started is reported as a failure, not a success.
- Codex now runs inside the macOS sandbox.

MemoryEx, continued

- Memories are saved as facts, not as orders. "You must…" style notes are rejected and rewritten as observations.
- Vague dates like "two weeks ago" or "last Monday" are flagged instead of saved as-is.
- Memory search now handles French accents.

Also in 3.0.2

- Several open terminals share work instead of repeating it, so the status bar uses less CPU.
- Model setup works on machines with custom providers.

top_items.content:
After two cycles with a 27B open-weights model, performance improved 1.2-1.6x per output token on tough research benchmarks (MLR-Bench, ScienceAgentBench, DSBench).

Multi-agent traces were also much better training data than single-agent ones, using fewer tokens to learn more.
